messages:
mike_customer: Hey team — our app started getting failures hitting the /v1/rerank endpoint. Example response: 
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
  Content-Type: application/json
  {
    \"error\": {
      \"type\": \"RERANK_INPUT_TOO_LARGE\",
      \"message\": \"input exceeds token limit\"
    }
  }
```
I'm pretty sure this happens only when the query is long OR when the doc set is large. We sent ~120 docs (avg 1.2k chars each) and the user query was ~3k chars. Can you advise what limits are and how to surface a clearer error to customers? This message doesn't tell which field to trim.

---

sara_support: Thanks for the report — sorry about the UX here. Can you paste a redacted example payload (query + doc lengths) and the time+org of the failed request? We can triage and open an engineer ticket. :pray:

mike_customer: Sure — redacted payload below. We replaced real text with Xs.
```
POST /v1/rerank
{
  \"query\": \"XXXXX...\"  // ~3,200 chars
  \"documents\": [\"XXXXX...\" x120] // longest ~4,500 chars
}
```
Request ID: req_01GkX... (org: acme-corp)  Timestamp: 2024-11-02T14:22:30Z

sara_support: Got it. Reassigning to eng. @nish_engineer can you look? Seems like both per-doc token and total token budget might be getting hit. Also UX: the error should indicate whether it's query vs docs vs total docs count.

nish_engineer: Looking. I pulled the logs using that request ID. Kernel shows: `rerank.total_input_tokens=28912`, `rerank.query_tokens=650`, `rerank.max_tokens_allowed=16384`, `rerank.num_docs=120`. So the total tokens exceed the configured 16k budget. The backend currently returns a generic RERANK_INPUT_TOO_LARGE with message "input exceeds token limit" (bad!), which the support team flagged last month too.

liam_devex: Re: messaging, customers frequently trim the query but the actual cause is too many/long docs. We should return structured guidance: which field exceeded, how many tokens we counted, and the limit. Eg: {\"error\": \"rerank.input_too_long\", \"field\": \"documents_total_tokens\", \"count\": 28912, \"limit\": 16384}. That will let SDKs show concise help and even auto-truncate with user consent.

nish_engineer: Agreed. Quick repro steps I used to validate locally: 
1) Create payload with a single query ~3k chars and 120 docs where each doc length is 4k chars.
2) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d @payload.json
The server returns 400 with the generic message. With an instrumented build I can add token counts to the error payload.

mike_customer: Appreciate that. Any ETA? Our customers are getting confused and support load is high. Also we hit unexpected UX with duplicates: some clients get a 400, others get an abort/timeout when we try to fragment the batch.

nish_engineer: I can push a small change to runtime to make the error include: `field`, `token_count`, `limit`, `num_docs`, and `max_docs_allowed`. That should be low-risk. Patch plan: 
- Add schema for new error: `rerank.input_too_long` with structured fields (backwards-compatible string `message` retained).
- Return `max_docs_allowed` (currently 100 for rerank by default) when `num_docs` exceeded.
- Include advisory `suggested_action` values: `truncate_docs`, `reduce_query`, `split_batch`.

liam_devex: Nice. Also request we update docs + SDKs to pre-flight-check via a helper `estimate_tokens` and throw client-side error before the network call. That reduces round trips. Could add a small sample snippet in the docs.

sara_support: For immediate mitigation, can we change the API error string to explicitly say e.g. "too many docs (120 > 100)" when docs count is the issue? Even if we don't add token counts yet, that would help triage.

nish_engineer: Yes — that's an easy server-side change. I'll open a PR to: 
- When `num_docs > max_docs` return 400 with `error.code: rerank.too_many_documents`, `error.message: "too many documents: 120 (max 100)"`.
- When `total_tokens > max_tokens` return `error.code: rerank.input_too_long` and include `token_count` and `limit` fields.
PR will add unit tests and a small migration note for clients. Planning to land in next sprint (ETA 4d).

mike_customer: That timeline works, though our team asked if there is a temporary workaround. We can pre-slice docs into multiple rerank calls but ordering is hard. Any quick server-side toggle?

nish_engineer: We could enable a soft-fail mode behind a flag that truncates docs automatically to fit the token budget and returns `truncated=true` with counts. But that has quality risks — I'd prefer explicit errors + clear guidance in docs for now. If you need immediate help, we can enable truncation for your org only (acme-corp) as a short-term toggle. Need approval from product.

liam_devex: I'll draft a snippet for the docs and a sample SDK helper: 
```
// JS helper
function preflightRerank(query, docs){
  const qTokens = estimate(query);
  const docsTokens = docs.map(d => estimate(d));
  if (docs.length > 100) throw new Error('too many documents (max 100)');
  if (qTokens + docsTokens.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0) > 16384) throw new Error('input exceeds token budget');
}
```
Add this to docs with recommendation for batching strategy: split into chunks of <=100 docs and keep per-chunk total tokens < 16384.

sara_support: Action items: 
- @nish_engineer open PR to improve error payload + unit tests (assignee: nish).
- @liam_devex update docs + add SDK preflight example (assignee: liam).
- Support to notify acme-corp (mike_customer) when soft-truncate toggle is available if they opt in.

nish_engineer: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/rerank-runtime/pull/542 — includes the structured error. I'll request review from eng-runtime.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued for canary channel: canary-20241107-17. Waiting automated checks. :rocket:

mike_customer: Thanks all — will share with product team. Please tag me once canary lands so we can validate with our real payloads.

sara_support: Will do. Marking thread for follow-up after canary. :eyes:

---
Notes for docs & product: Consider publishing a clear table of limits on rerank endpoint: max_docs (100), max_total_tokens (16,384), max_query_tokens (4,096 recommended), per_doc_max_tokens (8,192). These exact numbers are negotiable but documenting them will immediately cut support load.
